newsitem.title: UK: Iraq tells OPEC March crude output up 210,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Iraq tells OPEC March crude output up 210,000 bpd.

text.p: Iraq on Friday said it pumped 1.50 million barrels a day (bpd) of crude in March, up 210,000 bpd from 1.29 million in February, the OPEC news agency reported.
Iraq said its supply to the market, including domestic consumption, was 1.45 million bpd in March implying 50,000 bpd went into storage.
The data was provided in a monthly submission to OPEC headquarters in Vienna.
Iraqi output has been boosted since December by restricted sales under the U.N.'s humanitarian oil sale.
Prior to the oil sale, Baghdad said it was pumping 725,000 bpd for domestic consumption and small volumes trucked to Jordan.
Assuming domestic consumption and Jordanian sales remained unchanged then Iraqi exports in March rose to 725,000 bpd with a further 50,000 bpd going into storage.
Supply as defined by OPEC is calculated as domestic consumption, plus net export sales of crude and products, plus withdrawals of stocks held outside national boundaries.
